payload.name: Preserve explicit event facts during extraction
payload.description: When a message states a concrete past event with a time (who gave/received what, when), extract that event as a separate memory; do not let an interpretive summary replace it.
content: During extraction, treat explicit factual claims about past events (e.g., 'my parents got me this when I was 10') as distinct durable event memories with subject, kind, and time.

When the same utterance also supports an interpretation (e.g., 'it was the start of my passion'), keep the concrete event and the interpretation as separate memories; never let an interpretive summary substitute for the factual event.
Resolve relative time expressions (e.g., 'when I was 10') to an absolute world_start using the speaker's age at message time.

solves: The diagnosis showed extraction replacing a concrete, evidence-bound event (e.g., a parent giving a child an item at a specific age) with only an interpretive memory (e.g., the child developed an interest), losing the directly answerable fact. This skill applies to any future construction pass where a message states a specific past event with an explicit time: the factual event must be captured as its own memory even if an interpretive summary is also produced.
